transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Markus Lee (Citrine Head of ML), Sara O'Neil (CTO), Diego Ramos (DevOps), Jina Park (Product), Natalia Gomez (Security, joined late)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Customer is building an analytics platform that uses LLMs for summarization and entity extraction. They're evaluating Redwood for inference. Focus points: SDK integration, support for LangChain/LlamaIndex, how a gateway/proxy would sit in front of Redwood, rate limiting/quotas behavior, and observability hooks. Looking at hosted for quick start but want dedicated/private options for PII and latency.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, i have Priya our SE here too. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Markus: good thanks, hey Alex. i'm Markus, head of ML at Citrine. we have Sara and Diego on as well.
[00:10] Sara: hi all, thanks for fitting us in.
[00:14] Priya: hey, quick agenda — run through use case, current infra, integration approach (SDKs, langchain/llamaindex), gateway/proxy questions, rate limits and observability. then next steps. sound ok?
[00:22] Markus: yep. big picture — we ingest customer data and run summarization and entity extraction pipelines using fine-tuned models. latency target for interactive UI is 300-500ms p95 for short prompts, and bulk batch jobs overnight. data contains PII so we need controls.
[00:36] Diego: our infra is AWS, mostly EKS clusters, we run a Kong gateway in front of services and egress traffic is restricted via NAT and proxy.
[00:44] Alex: good, that helps. are you leaning hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, or private on VPC/on-prem at this stage?
[00:49] Sara: we'd like to try hosted to move fast, but we've got strict data residency/compliance concerns. may need dedicated or private for production.
[00:57] Priya: that's common. for hosted you get our standard retention and dedicated pools for predictable throughput. private gives you customer-managed networking and optional on-prem. we can map the tradeoffs after quick questions about traffic and latency.
[01:12] Markus: integration-wise — we use LangChain in our orchestration, and some teams use LlamaIndex for document stores. do you have adapters or examples?
[01:19] Priya: yes, we have SDKs in python/js and explicit examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors. i'll share snippets after the call. common pattern is to use our python client inside a LangChain LLM wrapper or use the LlamaIndex connector — works with streaming responses as well.
[01:33] Mark(approx): and about rate limits — how do quotas look if we have spikes? we want throttling to avoid cascading failures.
[01:40] Alex: good Q. hosted has tiered rate limits and token quotas per account; we can carve dedicated pools with higher per-second throughput and different quota configs. there are backpressure strategies — 429s, queueing and automatic fallback to smaller models to preserve availability.
[01:53] Diego: would that interact with our gateway? we have Kong doing auth and rate-limiting at the edge now. we want to keep a proxy in front for audit and egress control.
[02:01] Priya: totally supported. many customers put Redwood behind their gateway/proxy. we recommend a short-lived token scheme and connection keep-alives. if you need complete egress control, private deployment (VPC peering or on-prem) is the approach.
[02:15] Sara: about observability — we need traces and per-request metadata for cost allocation and debugging. do you provide hooks?
[02:21] Priya: yes — request-level logs, per-model token counts, latency breakdowns, and optional tracing integration (OpenTelemetry). you can push traces to your APM or pull logs via our audit exports. we also have per-route dashboards in Console.
[02:36] Markus: can we emit spans correlated to our request IDs? our debugging relies on that.
[02:40] Priya: yep we accept customer-supplied request IDs in headers and surface them in logs and traces. for high-volume workloads we recommend batch-level metadata to reduce overhead.
[02:51] Sara: on SDKs — what's the typical pattern for streaming vs non-streaming? we use streaming in UI.
[02:56] Priya: our SDKs support both. streaming uses server-sent events / websocket for low-latency tokens. streaming latency will depend on network hops; dedicated pools reduce added hops vs hosted global endpoints.
[03:10] Diego: network diagram question — if we keep Kong and our egress rules, does Redwood need any inbound changes? we prefer no open inbound from public internet.
[03:18] Alex: for hosted you call Redwood endpoints from your backend — no inbound to your private infra needed. for private/on-prem we offer a customer-managed control plane; that may require peering or an egress-friendly connector depending on the deployment model. Priya can follow up on exact network flows.
[03:33] Natalia (joined): sorry late, quick note — from security we need KMS integration for keys, audit logs retention, SOC2 artifact. what's your posture?
[03:41] Alex: we support KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated, audit logs with configurable retention (enterprise add-on), and we're SOC 2 Type II attested. we'll share the compliance pack.
[03:49] Natalia: ok thanks.
[03:52] Markus: can you share an example TCO for hosted vs dedicated? we want cost per 1k requests at our typical prompt sizes.
[03:58] Alex: yes i'll prepare an example TCO — we'll need your tokens per request distribution. also note quantization/ model selection affects cost.
[04:09] Priya: small technical note — we do automatic prefix and KV caching for repeated context; that can reduce token spend for chat-style flows. when using LangChain you can instrument caching at the retriever layer as well.
[04:23] Jina: are there recommended limits for concurrency per conv? like how many concurrent streams before degradation?
[04:28] Priya: it depends on model size and pool config. as a rule of thumb a medium dedicated pool supports N concurrent streams per GPU, and the platform auto-batches where it helps. we'll provide guidance for your traffic profile.
[04:40] Diego: about gateway auth — we use mTLS internally and the gateway performs SAML/SSO for user flows. can Redwood accept mTLS or only bearer tokens?
[04:49] Priya: currently we support bearer tokens (short-lived), but for private deployments we can do mutual TLS and SAML integrations for the admin console. we also support SSO/SAML for org access control and RBAC.
[05:01] Sara: any limits on custom headers or metadata size? we send contextual metadata per request for billing and routing.
[05:07] Priya: we support custom metadata headers up to a modest size (~4KB total) per request; large payloads are better sent as part of the body or stored in a referenced object store.
[05:18] Markus: ok, on benchmarking — we want to run a POC: 1) single-node hosted test to validate quality, 2) dedicated pool benchmark for latency, 3) private network trial for egress controls. is that doable?
[05:29] Alex: yes, typically we do a 4-week POC: week 1 onboarding + sample traffic, week 2 performance bench, week 3 integration and LangChain tests, week 4 handoff. we'll scope exact deliverables in the next doc.
[05:41] Diego: does the SDK support instrumentation for token counts so we can attribute cost back to product lines?
[05:46] Priya: yes SDK exposes token counts and we emit token-level cost attribution in Console. you can tag requests and use per-route breakdowns.
[05:55] Natalia: last compliance Q — can audit logs be forwarded to our SIEM, and are logs write-once?
[05:59] Alex: we provide log export connectors (S3/CloudWatch) and a push to syslog/ELK. write-once depends on your retention config but we can support append-only audit logs for enterprise packages. we'll include the options in the compliance pack.
[06:12] Priya: i will send LangChain/LlamaIndex snippets, streaming examples, and the observability hooks (OpenTelemetry example).
[06:17] Markus: great, that helps a lot.
[06:20] Alex: recap before we close — action items: i'll send hosted vs dedicated pricing and sample TCO; Priya will share SDK + LangChain examples and observability snippets; Diego to share gateway config; Natalia to confirm compliance scope; we schedule a technical deep dive next week to discuss private deployment network flows.
[06:38] Sara: sounds good, we'll send a sample prompt set and traffic profile.
[06:41] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[06:44] End

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of product names (e.g., LlamaIndex sometimes transcribed as 'Lama Index' in some chunks), timestamps approximate, speaker overlap minimal.
